minor.issue: Silent 5000-row cap (rows[:5000]) while 'received' reports the full row count and the UI copy says 'thousands of rows OK' — rows beyond 5000 are dropped with no error entry, so inserted+updated+error_count can be far less than received with no explanation.
Per-row await find_one + update_one (2 round-trips/row). 50 rows was fine, but large files will be slow; consider bulk_write/UpdateOne upserts.
Returns 200 {ok:true} even when no document matched (no 404), and still writes an audit entry.

issues: Recharts logs repeated console warnings 'The width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' on every data reload (ResponsiveContainer measured before layout). Cosmetic/log noise only — chart renders correctly; adding minHeight/explicit height would silence it.

action_items: Optional: report or raise the 5000-row import cap and include skipped rows in errors[] so counts reconcile with 'received'.
Optional: batch the import upserts with bulk_write for large files.
Optional: silence the recharts width/height console warnings on the Feedback Analytics chart.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1027 lines and mixes auth, ServiceNow, LLM/RAG, imports, CRUD factory and seed data — split into routers/services (>700 line guideline).

_build_context() loads entire historical/kb/rca collections into memory (to_list(20000)) and scores in Python on every analyze call; this is O(N) per analysis and will not scale past a few thousand rows — move to a Mongo text index / $search with a fallback.
Import path uses request.form() with the whole file read into memory (25 MB limit); consider streaming/chunked parsing for very large CSVs.
@app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown') is deprecated in current FastAPI — migrate to the lifespan context manager.
PostToServiceNow silently swallows 428 responses (relies on the global sn-creds-required event); if that listener ever unmounts the user gets no feedback at all — consider a fallback toast.
